name: AI agency
blurb: Sell AI-powered services such as content, chatbots or research to small businesses
title: How to Start an AI Agency: Services, Pricing and Risks
description: What an AI agency sells, how it charges clients, what you need to start, who it suits, the hype to ignore and how to test demand first.
h1: How to start an AI agency
answer: An AI agency sells finished work to businesses, such as written content, customer-service chatbots, image or video production or research, and uses AI tools to deliver it faster than a traditional agency. It earns project fees or monthly retainers. The catch is that clients pay for results, not for the tools, and anyone can open the same tools, so without a clear niche and real know-how it becomes a price race.

sections.h: How an AI agency makes money
body: Most agencies charge per project (build a support chatbot, produce a set of product photos), a monthly retainer for ongoing work (content, ads, reporting) or, less often, a share of measured results. The client pays for an outcome they can see; AI is how you keep your own hours down.

What eats the margin: tool subscriptions and API usage that grow with each client, revisions and fact-checking that AI output still needs, unpaid sales calls, and clients who leave once they learn to use the tools themselves.

ul: One service in one niche you understand, for example product descriptions for online shops or FAQ chatbots for clinics, rather than "AI for everyone".
Working skill in the trade itself (writing, design, marketing or support) so you can judge and fix what the tools produce.
A few paid tool accounts, kept to what the first service needs.
Two or three samples or a case study, even if done for free or for a friend's business.
A simple contract covering scope, revisions, who owns the output, and how client data is handled.
Business registration and tax setup as your country requires; some freelancers also carry professional liability insurance. Check local rules.

sections.h: Who it suits (and who it doesn't)

head: Suits
Not for
rows: People with a trade skill who want to deliver it faster
Anyone hoping the tools replace knowing the work
Good communicators comfortable with sales calls
People who dislike selling or client feedback
Someone with contacts in one industry
Those chasing every trend instead of one service

ul: Commodity pricing: if your offer is "we use AI", clients compare you with a cheap subscription. Sell a business result instead.
Accuracy and liability: AI output can be wrong, copied or off-brand. You are responsible for what you hand over, so review everything.
Client churn: retainers end when budgets tighten or clients bring the work in-house.

Course and template sellers: many "start an AI agency" programmes earn from students, not clients. Regulators such as the US Federal Trade Commission have acted against AI money-making schemes built on income claims.
Data and privacy: putting client data into third-party tools may break contracts or privacy law. Ask before you upload.

sections.h: How to test it cheaply first

ol: Pick one service and write a one-paragraph offer with a fixed price and delivery time.
Message ten businesses in your niche that you could help, and ask whether the problem matters to them.
Do one or two jobs at a reduced rate in exchange for a testimonial and permission to show the work.
Track how long each job really took, including revisions, and what the tools cost.
If nobody will pay even a small amount after twenty conversations, change the service or the niche before building a website.
Register the business, open a separate account and set up invoicing.
Write a short contract template and a client-data policy.
Build a one-page portfolio around your first case study.
Contact a few prospects every working day and log every reply.
Turn each delivery into a written checklist so the next one is faster.
Review pricing after your first three paying clients.

faq.q: Do I need to know how to code to run an AI agency?
faq.a: Not for most content, design or marketing services. You do need to understand the work well enough to judge quality. Chatbot and automation projects go more smoothly with some technical comfort, or a partner who has it.

faq.q: What is the difference between an AI agency and an AI automation agency?
faq.a: The terms overlap. An AI agency usually sells finished creative or marketing work made with AI, while an automation agency connects a client's software so routine tasks run on their own. Many small agencies do a little of both.

faq.q: How do AI agencies find clients?
faq.a: Mostly the slow way: personal networks, direct outreach to a narrow niche, referrals and showing real results. Paid courses that promise a client list are not a shortcut.
